title: Many Thomists reject Bellarmine's solution: God moves the will at his own choice, prior by nature to its self-determination
source_text: XVI. Verum ista Bellarmini solutio non placet multis eorum qui cum Thoma sentiunt, Voluntati, ut reliquis omnibus causis secundis, necessariam esse ad agendum praeviam quandam Dei motionem & applicationem. Statuunt enim Deum, absque ulla consideratione istiusmodi negativae determinationis quae in Voluntate creata praecesserit, Voluntatem pro suo arbitrio movere; neque movere simpliciter, sed ad sic, vel sic operandum efficaciter impellere: ita ut Voluntas ad hoc, & non aliud agendum, hoc volendum, illud nolendum a Deo determinetur, prius natura quam ipsa se determinet.
pass_a_gloss: But that solution of Bellarmine does not please many of those who think with Thomas, that a certain previous motion and application of God is necessary to the Will for acting, as to all other second causes. For they lay down that God, without any consideration of such a negative determination which may have preceded in the created Will, moves the Will at his own choice; and does not move it simply, but efficaciously impels it to operating thus, or thus: so that the Will is determined by God to doing this, and not another thing, to willing this, to refusing that, prior by nature than it determines itself.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine's solution does not satisfy many of those who hold with Thomas that the will, like every other secondary cause, needs a certain prior motion and application from God in order to act.

They maintain that God moves the will as he chooses, without any regard to a negative determination of that kind that may have preceded in the created will. He does not merely move it but efficaciously impels it to act in this way or that, so that the will is determined by God to do this and not something else, to will this and refuse that, first in the order of nature, before it determines itself.

lemmas.latin: prius natura quam ipsa se determinet
lemmas.gloss: prior by nature than it determines itself

choices.why: Kept as the Thomist technical term; Le Blanc explains 'physical' as opposed to 'moral', not to 'supernatural'.
